module
public import HexPrimality.Sieve
public meta import HexPrimality.Sieve
public import Lean
public section
#eval show IO Unit from do
  let input ← IO.mkRef (524289 : Nat)
  let bound ← input.get
  let state ← IO.mkRef (Hex.Nat.sieve bound (bound.sqrt + 1))
  let state ← state.get
  for block in [0:2] do
    for phase in (if block == 0 then [true, false] else [false, true]) do
      let start ← IO.monoNanosNow
      let ok ← if phase then do
        let output ← IO.mkRef (Hex.Nat.sieve bound (bound.sqrt + 1))
        let output ← output.get
        pure (output == state)
      else do
        let output ← IO.mkRef (Hex.Nat.bitsToList state bound)
        let output ← output.get
        pure (output.length == 43388)
      let stop ← IO.monoNanosNow
      IO.println ((Lean.Json.mkObj [("block", Lean.toJson block),
        ("phase", Lean.toJson (if phase then "sieve" else "readback")),
        ("nanos", Lean.toJson (stop - start)), ("ok", Lean.toJson ok)]).compress)
interpretation: Readback timings are retained. Sieve timing is invalid: the repeated pure sieve expression was shared with the prepared state before the clock. These sieve rows are diagnostic only and are excluded from performance claims.
